correctness.rationale: The multinomial enumeration at t-1 requires exactly q-1 copies of the terminal label, at least q of the others, and arbitrary null count; this gives the labeled coefficient formula, with strictly positive masses for all t>=mq. For a pair i,j, the shared coefficient sequence is log-concave with interval support, including the point mass when m=2 and p_0=0. Its Toeplitz minors are nonnegative by decreasing ratios; convolution follows by finite Cauchy–Binet. For p_i>p_j, the two remaining coupon columns have strictly positive minors in the stated order on indices r,s>=q. For adjacent output rows n,n+1, the choice r=n-h, s=r+1 at the first supported index h makes the Toeplitz minor exactly a_h^2>0. Thus the ordering is strict, and time normalization does not alter the odds. Counting a single extra draw gives the displayed mq+1 posterior. Exchangeability and those first two posteriors give the independence criterion. Pairwise odds comparisons imply strict decrease of the mean of any strictly increasing g(p_J) when rates differ; the independent-copy covariance identity gives the sign. Finally, conditional on exactly q-1 copies of i before completion, the remaining quotas are met with probability tending to one, leaving the slowest factor (1-p_i)^(t-q) for minimal rates. Ties are exchangeable. Independent exact word enumeration for q=3 and probabilities (1,3,4)/8 gave posteriors (1/3,1/3,1/3), (7/16,5/16,1/4), (160/303,88/303,55/303), verifying the successive minors in that case.
residual_risks: The independent replay is finite and uses no null draws; coverage of null draws and all quotas is analytical.

evidence: May's completion law sums over the label that meets its quota on the last draw; individual summands give terminal-label masses with heterogeneous quotas. Anceaume et al. treat unmarked completion times for distinct coupons including a null type.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A heterogeneous-quota coefficient law implies the analogous labeled law at equal quotas without a null type but does not itself state the strict inequality; an unmarked completion-time theorem cannot supply terminal-label odds. The full strict equal-quota coverage is instead explicit in 49ad21f71f59.

evidence: 49ad21f71f59 already gives the labeled EGF, earliest uniformity, strict MLR and asymptotic pairwise odds; the proof uses the same Toeplitz and log-concavity setting.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One extra coefficient of the prior joint law gives the mq+1 posterior; independence follows from strict odds when nonuniform and symmetry otherwise. Standard expectation monotonicity for the already established odds and the covariance identity give the sign. The prior asymptotic odds imply concentration on minimum rates with uniform ties. These consequences do not establish a new ordering.

value.rationale: A sharp terminal-label ordering across all times would be a useful structural result. Here that ordering is already stated for the full model, and the extra mq+1 expression, independence and covariance are elementary consequences of the same exact law and ordering. The record does not resolve another meaningful gap beyond the known theorem.
residual_risks: No assessment of possible extensions to unequal quotas or dependent draws, which are outside the frozen claim.
